mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate relative to its recent trend compresses equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days without regime dependency.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in 60% or more of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 0.1% (rolling 3-month average).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in unemployment rate below 8.0% signals strengthening labor market conditions, which correlates with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in 60% or more of months where UNRATE falls below 8.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts and industrial production (both above their 6-month moving averages) indicates robust economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction signal (both HOUST and INDPRO above 6mo_avg) fails to predict positive 60-day returns in 60% or more of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL above 3.0% annualized), the market prices in aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in 60% or more of high inflation regime periods (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%).

mechanism_narrative: Strong retail sales (RSAFS) indicate robust consumer spending, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days without regime dependency.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in 60% or more of instances where RSAFS is above its 3-month average.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly employment growth rate exceeding 0.5% signals a rapidly improving labor market, which correlates with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in 60% or more of months with PAYEMS growth above 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in the federal funds rate and unemployment rate (both exceeding 0.25% and 0.1% monthly drops, respectively) signal a dovish monetary policy combined with a strong labor market, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (FEDFUNDS down >0.25% and UNRATE down >0.1%) fails to predict positive 60-day returns in 60% or more of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In supply shock regimes (INDPRO below 95.0), economic output contraction leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate profitability.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in 60% or more of periods when INDPRO is below 95.0.
